subject: Startups
title: Growth at All Costs
description: A fast breakdown of Growth at All Costs for builders.

hook.text: WeWork grew to 800 locations in 120 cities. Then its IPO collapsed, revealing a company that mistook growth for health.

buildup.text: In the 2010s, VCs rewarded 'blitzscaling': grow as fast as possible, worry about profits later.

discovery.text: Companies burned billions chasing user numbers. Uber lost $8 billion before going public.

twist.text: But growth without unit economics is renting customers with VC money. When funding stops, the customers leave.

climax.text: After 2022, VCs demanded profitability. 'Grow at all costs' became 'grow efficiently.' The era of cheap money ended.

punchline.text: Growth isn't a strategy. Profitable growth is.

quiz.question: What major shift happened in startup funding after 2022?
options: Demand shifted from growth to profitability
